analysis.summary: This PR introduces several high-severity functional bugs including runtime crashes in filtering logic, incorrect type handling in file uploads, and a regression in error interception that could mask integration failures.

bugs.title: Runtime crash in order filtering logic
bugs.description: The logic `order[option.code]?.toUpperCase().includes(...)` performs optional chaining on the property access but then immediately calls `.includes()` on the result of `toUpperCase()`. If the property is null or missing, `toUpperCase()` returns `undefined`, and calling `.includes()` on `undefined` will throw a TypeError.
bugs.risk: High. The application will crash whenever a user attempts to filter the order list if any order object is missing the expected filter key (e.g., during the transition to showroom car types).

bugs.title: Invalid type coercion in document upload
bugs.description: The code converts a file to a Base64 string and then uses a TypeScript cast (`as File`) to treat that string as a File object before passing it to an Axios POST request. A raw string is not a valid substitute for a File/Blob object in binary or multipart uploads.
bugs.risk: High. Document uploads will fail at runtime in local/dev environments (where the 4000/ port condition is met) because the backend will receive a string instead of a valid multipart file stream.

bugs.title: Regression in error interception logic
bugs.description: The error handler was changed to look for `data.error` instead of the standard `data.errors?.[0]` array. Most GraphQL and Mulesoft integration responses return an array of errors. By switching to a single object lookup, the middleware will fail to extract error details from existing backend services.
bugs.risk: High. Critical error context from Salesforce and Mulesoft will be lost, causing the UI to display a generic 'system error' instead of actionable feedback for agents (e.g., validation failures).

bugs.title: PR Scope Violation: Unrelated build infrastructure changes
bugs.description: The PR title and context focus on the 'showroom' feature release, yet it introduces a significant change to the project's `.npmrc`, switching the registry to an Aliyun-specific local NPM path.
bugs.risk: High. This is a configuration leak that can break dependency resolution and build pipelines for developers outside the specific local environment where this was tested.

notBugs.reason: While calling a presigned URL with global axios headers is risky, there is no evidence in the diff that a global axios interceptor injecting auth headers exists; the project may be using clean instances.
Although the case changed from 'appointmentId' to 'AppointmentId', the corresponding test mocks were also updated, suggesting an intentional alignment with a new AWS backend contract.
Speculative risk; while hardcoded SOQL queries are brittle, there is no definitive proof in the diff that 'Customer_ID__c' and 'outletId' are mismatched for this specific project schema.
